title: Fixed stars: SWIEPH + JPL backend support for fixstar2
description:
## Summary
Extend the star position pipeline (`calc_fixstar`, landed in swisseph-rs/55 for Moshier) to the **SWIEPH** and **JPL** backends, so `fixstar2`/`_ut`/`_mag` work for all three ephemeris sources. The star math is backend-independent except for obtaining the observer (Earth heliocentric/barycentric) position at Step 5/6; this sub-task generalizes that one seam and adds golden coverage. Mirrors the `calc_planet` / `calc_planet_sweph` / `calc_planet_jpl` structure already in `calc.rs`.

## Files
- `src/calc.rs` — generalize `calc_fixstar`'s observer retrieval (Step 5/6) to dispatch per backend, or add thin `calc_fixstar_sweph` / `calc_fixstar_jpl` wrappers that supply the Earth/Sun positions and delegate to the shared star math. Factor the shared 18-step math so all three backends reuse it.
- `src/context.rs` — in `fixstar2`, dispatch on `self.config.ephemeris_source` and pass the right backend handles (`self.planet_files` / `self.moon_files` / `self.jpl_file`) into the appropriate `calc_fixstar*`, matching how `calc_inner` dispatches `calc_body_{sweph,jpl,moshier}`.
- `tests/c-gen/gen_fixstar.c` (extend) + `tests/golden-data/fixstar.json` + `tests/golden/fixstar.rs` (extend with SWIEPH/JPL cases).

## Implementation steps
1. Study how `calc_planet_sweph` / `calc_planet_jpl` obtain Earth positions: `calc::sweph_positions` returns `SwephPositions { planet_bary, earth_bary, earth_helio, sun_bary }`; the JPL path uses `JplProvider`. Identify the exact Earth pos+vel (and Sun, for deflection) each backend yields, matching C `main_planet_bary(SEI_EARTH, …)` for that source.
2. Refactor `calc_fixstar` so the 18-step math (swisseph-rs/55) takes the observer Earth position (and Sun, implicitly at origin for the deflection geometry) as an input, and add per-backend front-ends that compute that observer position. Keep the Moshier path identical to swisseph-rs/55.
3. Wire `Ephemeris::fixstar2` to call the source-appropriate front-end.

## C reference
`docs/c-ref-fixstar.md` §"Position Computation" (Step 5/6 observer), §"Public Entry Points". Cross-reference `calc_planet_sweph`/`calc_planet_jpl` in `src/calc.rs`.

## Golden tests
- Extend `tests/c-gen/gen_fixstar.c` to emit cases with `SEFLG_SWIEPH` and `SEFLG_JPLEPH` (de441.eph) for the same star/epoch matrix as swisseph-rs/55 (a representative subset is fine: Sirius, Spica, `,SgrA*` × J2000, 1900, 2050 × {base, |SPEED, |EQUATORIAL}).
- Extend `tests/golden/fixstar.rs` with test fns building `Ephemeris` for `EphemerisSource::Swiss` (`ephe_path = ../swisseph/ephe`) and `EphemerisSource::Jpl` (`jpl_filename = de441.eph`). Tolerances as swisseph-rs/55: positions 1e-8, speeds 1e-6.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cargo test --test golden fixstar -- --nocapture` passes including the new SWIEPH/JPL cases.
- `cargo build` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.

## Escape hatch
If SWIEPH/JPL positions exceed 1e-8 after two attempts, STOP and report failing cases (actual vs expected) and what you tried; the observer-position seam (barycentric vs heliocentric per backend) is the likely cause. Escalate to Opus.
